descriptions.github:5673460619: Current behavior If an EffectiveViewportChanged handler throws, layout is permanently wedged. Every later layout pass throws a NullReferenceException from EventManager.RaiseEffectiveViewportChangedEvents , so new content never gets Loaded and the window stops updating. From the log of the repro below: The first exception is the handler's own. The NREs are the bug: they come from Uno's queue handling, not from user code, and never stop. WinUI's CLayoutManager::RaiseEffectiveViewportChangedEvents ( src/dxaml/xcp/core/layout/LayoutManager.cpp ) walks the queue without modifying it and clears it afterwards, so it never leaves the queue half consumed. descriptions.github:5673427734: Current behavior 🐛 BorderVisual (Skia) replaces its RectangleClip objects whenever the border or corner radius geometry changes, but never disposes the old ones. In UpdatePathsAndCornerClip() , the old childClipCausedByCornerRadius and backgroundClip are just set to null and new clips are created (L203-L212, L330-L346). Since 24230, RectangleClip caches one geometry (a native SKPath ) and only releases it in DisposeInternal() (RectangleClip.skia.cs L42). Nothing calls Dispose() on a replaced clip, so its cached path is freed only by the SKPath finalizer when the GC gets around to it, not deterministically. Impact is low: it is bounded to one path per replaced clip and the finalizer does clean it up eventually. It can only pile up between GCs, for example while a rounded Border is being resized or animated frame after frame. This was confirmed by code inspection on master (7a2214115d5)…

descriptions.github:5670597517: Summary OWON CM2100B support was built from OWON's manuals, OWON's iMeter Android app and OWON's PC software, and has never been tested against a CM2100B . Key finding: OWON's Bluetooth meters advertise the name BDM and, once connected, stream a 6-byte reading on characteristic FFF4 with no request; the model code the tool reads from characteristic FFF2 when it connects picks the entry, and no cable or pairing is needed. descriptions.github:5670511660: docs/CONTRIBUTING.md tells contributors to run three commands before pushing: ruff check, ruff format --check, and pytest. The CI check job also runs mypy over taken/, which the contributor list omits. A contributor following the doc would be surprised by a CI failure they could have caught locally. Evidence: - docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:41 - .github/workflows/ci.yml Expected behavior: Add mypy to the pre-push command list in docs/CONTRIBUTING.md. Why it matters: A contributor following the doc gets a surprise CI failure they could have caught locally. The doc should match the pipeline. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670510748: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/CONTRIBUTING.md both describe the vendored-console-copy rule and give a re-copy command, but both only mention checks.py and verdict.py. The CI docs-sync job checks three pairs, including taken/budget.py vs docs/console/py/budget.py. A contributor editing taken/budget.py who follows only the docs would not re-copy it, and only CI would catch the drift. Evidence: - docs/ARCHITECTURE.md - docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:47 - .github/workflows/ci.yml Expected behavior: Update the re-copy commands in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/CONTRIBUTING.md to include taken/budget.py, matching the three pairs CI actually checks. Why it matters: A contributor who follows only the docs would drift the vendored copy and learn about it from a red CI run instead of the docs. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670510245: The Modules section of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md lists cli.py, checks.py, verdict.py, graphql.py, discover.py, and mcp server.py, but omits taken/budget.py (API budget tiers, worker sizing) and taken/health.py (the --health maintainer report). Since the doc is the contributor map for the codebase, a new contributor has no pointer to where health or budget logic lives. Evidence: - docs/ARCHITECTURE.md Expected behavior: Add taken/budget.py and taken/health.py to the Modules section of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md with one-line descriptions. Why it matters: The architecture doc is the contributor map of the codebase. Two whole subsystems are missing from it. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670509839: The JSON output section in README.md (byte-identical to docs/index.md) says taken --json owner/repo 123 prints an object with three keys, but taken/cli.py emits five: target, verdict, reasons, findings, budget. It also documents a stars field inside repo health , but taken/checks.py builds repo health with keys pushed at, pushed recently, recent merges, contributors, and contributors window days, with no stars key. Anyone writing a script against the documented schema would look for a field that never appears. Evidence: - docs/index.md:159 - docs/index.md:171 - taken/cli.py:660 - taken/checks.py:1447 Expected behavior: Fix the documented key count (five, not three) and remove the nonexistent stars field from the repo health docs, or add the field if it is meant to exist. Why it matters: Anyone scripting against the documented JSON schema builds on a false contract. The docs are a…

descriptions.github:5670508937: Problem open output folder() contains separate behavior for Windows, macOS, and Linux, but the platform-specific branches do not currently have focused unit-test coverage. A regression in command selection or failure handling could therefore go unnoticed even though --open-folder is a documented user-facing option. Requested behavior Add deterministic unit tests for the platform-specific behavior of open output folder() . Cover at least: - Windows using os.startfile() ; - macOS using open ; - Linux using xdg-open ; - Linux when xdg-open cannot be found; - opener/subprocess failures producing a warning instead of crashing. The tests should mock platform and process-launch behavior rather than actually opening folders. Current workaround The option is covered indirectly through parsing/workflow tests, but its platform-specific launch behavior is primarily exercised manually. Relevant code…
descriptions.github:5670508946: docs/takendocs.md is an auto-generated CLI reference (per scripts/gen cli reference.py, which runs taken --help ), but the checked-in copy is stale. Compared with taken/cli.py, it omits ten flags: --allocation, --explore-floor, --health, --claim-wait-days, --pr-stale-days, --gfi-stale-days, --rest, --pr-idle-days, --claim-silence-days, --claim-silence-complex-days. The --graphql help text is also outdated: the page says it is opt-in, while the current CLI says GraphQL is the default for logged-in users and falls back to REST on failure. A user reading the docs-site CLI reference will never learn these flags exist. The regeneration step is mentioned nowhere except the page header itself, which is how it went stale. Evidence: - docs/takendocs.md:11 - docs/takendocs.md:52 - taken/cli.py - scripts/gen cli reference.py Expected behavior: Regenerate docs/takendocs.md from the current CLI…
descriptions.github:5670508013: In run gql attempt, when the gh subprocess exits nonzero and stderr is empty, the raised error is ' gh api graphql failed: ' with nothing after the colon. The user gets no actionable detail about what failed. Expected: fall back to the return code or stdout content when stderr is empty, so the message always names the failure. Evidence: - taken/graphql.py:227 - taken/graphql.py:252 Expected behavior: Fall back to the return code or stdout content when stderr is empty, so the raised error always names the failure. Why it matters: An error message that ends at the colon is a dead end for anyone debugging at 2am. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670507157: The --limit help text says 'max open issues to check per owner/repo scan target', which is true for scan mode. But --discover passes args.limit into DiscoverOptions(limit=...), where limit means max candidates returned, a different semantic. The MCP discover candidates tool documents the correct semantic ('Max candidates to return'). Expected: the CLI help should name both semantics, or the discover path should get its own flag wording. A user tuning --discover --limit 5 expecting 5 issues per repo instead gets at most 5 candidates total. Evidence: - taken/cli.py:74 - taken/cli.py:483 Expected behavior: Name both semantics in the --limit help text, or give the discover path its own flag wording. Why it matters: A user tuning --discover --limit 5 expecting five issues per repo gets five candidates total. That is a usability trap sitting in the flagship mode. Found during an automated…
descriptions.github:5670506268: --jobs is validated (--jobs must be at least 1, exit 3), and the decay-day flags use non negative int, but --limit and --min-contributors use plain type=int: --limit -5 silently scans zero issues and exits 0 with a 'no open issues found' note, and --min-contributors -3 is silently meaningless. --explore-floor takes any float even though it is a probability (default 0.15). The same gap exists on the MCP side: discover candidates accepts negative pr idle days / claim silence days / claim silence complex days with no validation, and scan repo(limit=-5) returns an all-zero summary indistinguishable from a genuinely empty repo. Expected: the same non-negative (and range) validation the codebase already applies to the other numeric inputs. Evidence: - taken/cli.py:74 - taken/cli.py:98 - taken/cli.py:126 - taken/cli.py:50 - taken/mcp server.py:157 - taken/mcp server.py:252 Expected behavior…
descriptions.github:5670505846: Unparseable targets go through parse error, which deliberately returns exit code 3 (the code comments that a usage error must exit 3 without touching the network). But --discover given targets and --health given bad targets go through argparse parser.error, which exits 2. Scripts or agents that distinguish exit 3 as the usage-error contract get mixed signals depending on which flag was misused. Expected: one consistent exit code for all usage errors. This is low impact since both codes are nonzero, but the codebase states its own contract and then violates it in two paths. Evidence: - taken/cli.py:41 - taken/cli.py:372 - taken/cli.py:378 - taken/cli.py:380 Expected behavior: Use one consistent usage-error exit code across all CLI paths, matching the documented contract of 3 from the parse error comment. Why it matters: Scripts and agents key off exit codes, including our own scout…
descriptions.github:5670504865: The scan issue claims docstring describes a claim as waiting when it is older than claim wait days, but waiting entry and quiet entry return entries when age days == wait days (they only reject age days < wait days). The inclusive boundary is arguably the better behavior, but the docstring and code disagree by one day; pick one and make both match. Evidence: - taken/health.py:212 - taken/health.py:178 - taken/health.py:196 Expected behavior: Pick one boundary and make the docstring match the code. The inclusive code behavior looks like the right one to keep. Why it matters: One-day disagreements between docs and code are exactly how the next contributor introduces a real off-by-one. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670503339: truncated is computed as len(issues) = options.issue limit, so a repo with exactly issue limit open issues and nothing more is flagged as truncated even though the listing is complete. The flag should only be set when there is evidence of more data, for example when a full final page was returned. Minor, but it can send a maintainer looking for issues that do not exist. Evidence: - taken/health.py:349 Expected behavior: Set truncated only when there is evidence of more data, for example a full final page, instead of the = comparison against issue limit. Why it matters: A false truncated flag sends a maintainer hunting for issues that do not exist. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670501677: pace search is defined but never called anywhere in the audited files; the live pacing path is wait search pace called from gh api run while holding search lock. Dead code carrying a docstring that describes live behavior risks a future reader wiring it in (which would double-pace searches) or relying on behavior that is never exercised. It should be removed or covered by a test that pins the intended pacing contract. Evidence: - taken/checks.py:437 Expected behavior: Remove the dead helper, or pin it with a test if it is meant to be the future pacing contract. It should not sit there looking live while nothing calls it. Why it matters: Dead code with a live-sounding docstring misleads the next reader into wiring it in, which would double-pace searches. Keep the codebase honest. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670443975: Current scene appears to have a scale mismatch between the VR player and vehicles, with the player appearing significantly larger than the cars. Since measurement system records distances, speeds and TTC, inconsistent object scale could make the recorded measurements invalid. TODOs - 1 Unity unit = metre. - Verify vehicle dimensions against realistic dimensions. - Verify road, footpath, kerb, lane and crossing dimensions - Check that vehicle/ player colliders match their visible geometry. - Check height/pos of VR relative to participant. - Verify all recorded distances are expressed correctly in metres. - Verify all recorded times are expressed correctly in seconds. - Verify that the halfway pause is measured and removed in seconds. - add a simple documneted scale reference to the scene for dev. - run a test scenario and confirm that the resulting CSV values are physically plausible.
descriptions.github:5670440609: Goal The web app ships as its own container image instead of inside the server's jar, so it deploys and scales on its own. This is part of E03 Module boundaries. Steps 1. Add web/apps/web/Dockerfile . A build stage with Node and pnpm copies shared/openapi.yaml and web/ , runs pnpm install --frozen-lockfile and pnpm build . A serve stage uses a small unprivileged static server, such as nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged , serves web/apps/web/dist , and falls back to index.html for every unknown path, so links into the app work. 2. Remove the web stage from server/Dockerfile , and the static/ copy with it. 3. In shared/deploy/chart/templates/ , add a web Deployment and Service. In ingress.yaml , route /api , /oauth , and /.well-known to the server, and / to the web app. 4. In shared/deploy/compose.yaml , add a web service. Compose has no ingress, so its server config forwards /api , /oauth , and…
descriptions.github:5670430769: The Vietnamese phrases were machine-translated, and their audio is AI-generated. Nobody fluent in Vietnamese has checked them yet. If you speak Vietnamese fluently, go through the 12 categories in the app and check that: - each phrase is correct, and sounds natural for a traveler talking to a stranger - the audio pronounces it the way a native speaker would Report problems with the wrong translation or audio forms, or fix them directly in src/data/translations/vi.json (see CONTRIBUTING.md). Please comment here before you start, so two people don't review the same language at once. Worth checking first: - The phrases use Northern (Hanoi) vocabulary and pronunciation. - "Cheers!" is "Một, hai, ba, dô!", with a colloquial spelling. - "Police" is "công an", and "metro station" is "Ga tàu điện ngầm". - Tones matter a lot in Vietnamese, so listen to the audio closely.

descriptions.github:5670344064: Problem yaatv currently emits its low-bitrate source warning whenever the detected bitrate is below the configured threshold. That warning is useful for lossy sources such as MP3 or AAC, but it can be misleading for lossless formats such as FLAC, ALAC, WAV, or AIFF. A lossless source can have a comparatively low bitrate because of its content or compression efficiency without representing degraded source quality. Requested behavior Only emit the low-bitrate source-quality warning when the source codec/format is one where bitrate is a meaningful quality signal. The change should: - preserve the existing warning for applicable lossy sources; - avoid the warning for clearly lossless sources such as FLAC, ALAC, WAV, and AIFF; - keep the existing warning threshold unchanged; - add focused unit tests for both lossy and lossless cases; - preserve --no-warn behavior. Current workaround Users of…

descriptions.github:5670236246: Problem When yaatv generates the default output filename, it reads artist/title metadata from the audio file. The current artist lookup recognizes values such as artist , albumartist , ID3 TPE1 , and MP4 ©ART , but some supported containers expose equivalent artist metadata under other common keys. In particular: - MP4/M4A can use aART for album artist; - ASF/WMA commonly uses Author . When those are the only populated artist fields, yaatv can fall back to the source filename instead of producing the expected Artist - Title.mp4 default name. Requested behavior Extend artist metadata lookup so the default output-name path also recognizes the relevant MP4 and ASF/WMA artist aliases. At minimum: - recognize MP4 aART ; - recognize ASF/WMA Author ; - preserve the current precedence for existing artist fields; - keep title handling unchanged unless a format-specific test shows a corresponding…

Users migrating to the native app would love their playlists to travel with them — and the format is fully documented in the old code, so no guesswork is needed. What to do - Single PR: "import backup" entry point (paste-from-clipboard, mirroring the legacy UX) that parses the JSON above, validates formatVersion , and matches each songId against the current device MediaStore library. - Songs not found on this device must be reported, not silently dropped (e.g. "3 of 42 songs not…

descriptions.github:5670083422: Context The web version ( legacy branch) stored favorites as a playlist literally named "favoritos" (id 1). The native app inherited the hack: playlists.kt hardcodes a "favoritos" sentinel row. If the user renames that playlist, favorites silently "disappear", and any playlist the user names favoritos collides with it. What to do When introducing Room (see the playlists persistence issue), model this properly instead of porting the sentinel: - playlists table gets a kind column: NORMAL / FAVORITES , with a constraint/guarantee that exactly one FAVORITES row exists. - Migration path: a legacy row named "favoritos" becomes kind = FAVORITES , not a name match. - Export keeps writing name: "favoritos", id: 1 in the backup JSON, so backups produced by the new app remain readable by the old app (forward compat for free). Scope - Part of the Room playlists work: decide kind vs alternatives in…
descriptions.github:5670078564: Spike to investigate a better implementation of history state for agents/MCP. Based on conversation in 68 On "not ideal": one alternative keeps the change undoable in Edit mode. Undo.undo() and redo() apply a selection entry when entry.selection before instanceof UndoSystem.selectionSave , and they only call its load() . A subclass that snapshots the texture's own selection (by UUID) and restores it in load() doesn't depend on UVEditor.texture : I tried it live with risky eval , in Edit mode with nothing in the UV editor. Undo cleared the 16 selected pixels and kept the texture, and Redo brought them back. The trade-off: it relies on UndoSystem.selectionSave and on pushing to Undo.history directly, with the same bookkeeping as finishSelection (trim the redo branch, undo limit , index ). It should also record nothing when Undo Selection is off or in an Edit Session, like the native path…

descriptions.github:5669910043: The gap docs/architecture/overview.md lists this under Known gaps , added in 2140: The retry wait() in workspace-changes.ts never removes its abort listener when its timer fires, so a stream that keeps dropping, as it does while the API is down, adds one listener to the workspace's signal per attempt, about 360 an hour, until the last list leaves. It also waits out its timer when the signal is already aborted, so a stream torn down between attempts takes up to 10 seconds to stop. Why it matters The sources panel and the Studio list share this one stream per workspace since 2126, and it reconnects whenever it drops: the API restarts, the machine sleeps, the sidecar crashes. While the API stays down, follow() retries every 10 seconds, and each retry's wait() leaves a closure on the signal, holding its timer and its settled promise, until the workspace is left. Nothing breaks and nothing…

descriptions.github:5669640859: Goal Add a small check for broken or malformed external references in maintained skill and README documentation. Acceptance criteria - Restrict checks to relevant checked-in Markdown files and HTTP(S) references. - Report the file and URL for failures; handle redirects and fragments without treating a valid page as broken. - Keep the default validator usable with the Python standard library; document any optional network check separately. - Provide a deterministic offline test or fixture for URL extraction and reporting behavior. - Do not make CI network checks flaky or fail silently on transient network errors. Avoid automatically rewriting links; report actionable results for a contributor to review.
descriptions.github:5669640596: Goal Add a concise, tool-neutral scorecard template that helps teams define a RAG evaluation before comparing pipeline changes. Acceptance criteria - Include dataset version, query, expected answer or claims, expected sources, answerability, and access-control context. - Include retrieval, grounding/citation, answer quality, latency, and cost measures where applicable. - Explain that metric definitions and thresholds must be selected for the use case; do not imply one aggregate score proves production readiness. - Provide brief scoring instructions and an example row using synthetic content. - Link to primary metric documentation where the template names a specific metric. Do not add a vendor dependency or sensitive example data.
descriptions.github:5669640738: Goal Add a short troubleshooting section for when a skill is installed but an agent does not discover or invoke it. Acceptance criteria - Cover the documented paths for OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code. - Include checks for the SKILL.md frontmatter, folder/skill name, project versus global placement, active working directory, and restarting or refreshing the session where appropriate. - Link discovery behavior to each client's current official documentation. - Clearly label client-specific details and avoid assuming undocumented behavior is universal. Keep the section practical and concise.
descriptions.github:5669640370: Goal Create a small, clearly synthetic MCP server example with a few intentional review findings, then show how a generic review differs from a review guided by mcp-engineering and security-review . Acceptance criteria - Keep the server and data fictional; include no credentials, customer data, or live target. - Use the same prompt and code in both example conditions. - Tie findings to exact code and distinguish confirmed defects from context-dependent risks. - Label the outputs as illustrative unless they are actual, reproducible model runs. - Cover relevant MCP concerns such as tool authorization, input validation, output handling, and logging without claiming the example is exhaustive. Follow the project's contributing and security-scope guidance.
descriptions.github:5669640230: Goal Check Cursor's current official documentation for Agent Skills support and add installation guidance only if the supported discovery path is clear. Acceptance criteria - Link to the current official Cursor documentation and note when it was checked. - Document the verified project and/or user skill path and any relevant discovery limitations. - Keep Cursor optional; do not change the existing OpenCode, Codex, or Claude Code installers. - If support cannot be established from primary sources, record the uncertainty instead of guessing. Keep the change focused on documentation and avoid claims based only on third-party posts.
descriptions.github:5669579562: What happened? The COMPOSABLE scoring tent currently penalizes modules with extreme stability ($I = 0.00$), dropping their score to 0%. While this penalty makes sense for high-level orchestration modules, it creates a false positive penalty for leaf utility files (e.g., basic UI components, data structures, or primitive helpers) that are intended to have zero efferent coupling ($C e = 0$). Example Scenario 1. Additional features adopt menu.rs , raising afferent coupling ($C a \ge 2$). 3. Because menu.rs relies on no other internal modules ($C e = 0$), its instability now resolves to $I = 0.00$. 4. Result: Topos penalizes the file for extreme stability, dropping its score from 80% to 0.0% and triggering a…

descriptions.github:5669261268: Problem - Users walk away from slow requests. Local models are slow, so users switch to something else during long requests and don't know when one finishes or needs approval. - Long-running processes block the model. It can't start a dev server or a test watcher and keep working, because bash waits for the command to end, or times out. Proposal - Notifications: a desktop notification when a request that took longer than N seconds finishes, or when it waits for approval. - It uses notify-send on Linux and osascript on macOS, with the terminal bell as a fallback. - Settings: notify = on | off and the time threshold. - Good first issue. - Background commands: bash with background: true starts a process and returns an id. - bash output(id) reads its new output and bash stop(id) stops it. - Background processes are stopped when the session ends and listed in /jobs . Acceptance criteria - […
descriptions.github:5669260363: Problem Many developers want the agent inside their editor, where they can see diffs inline, accept or reject changes, and share the current selection. Proposal - The Agent Client Protocol (ACP): implement its agent side. lcode acp speaks ACP over stdio, so editors that support ACP can run lcode as their agent, with the editor's own diff review and approval UI. - Mapping: lcode's tools, approvals, checkpoints and MCP servers map onto ACP. Edits go through the editor's buffers. - Later: a dedicated VS Code extension, if ACP support there isn't enough. Acceptance criteria - [ ] lcode acp works with at least one ACP editor (for example Zed), with diffs and approvals in the editor - [ ] Documented, with setup per editor
descriptions.github:5669259533: Problem lcode only talks to Ollama. Many people run LM Studio, llama.cpp's llama-server , vLLM on a workstation, or MLX on a Mac, which is often faster on Apple Silicon. Proposal - A backend interface, plus an OpenAI-compatible backend (chat completions with streaming and tool calls). It covers LM Studio, llama-server , vLLM and MLX servers ( mlx lm.server , or LM Studio's MLX engine). - Configuration: backend = "ollama" | "openai" and base url . These are memory-fit estimates, the /context picker, unloading for free gpu , and vision checks. - Benchmarks: lcode bench works with every backend, so you can compare, for example, Ollama and MLX on the same Mac. Acceptance criteria - [ ] lcode works end to end with LM…
descriptions.github:5669258945: Problem On an unfamiliar codebase, the model spends many steps and tokens discovering its structure. grep finds exact words, not ideas such as "where do we retry failed uploads?". Proposal - Repository map: a compact, ranked outline of the repository's important symbols (classes, functions, signatures, extracted with tree-sitter). - Symbols are ranked by how often they're referenced, like aider's repo map, and the map is cut to a token budget. - Small repositories get it in the system prompt; larger ones through a repo map tool. - Semantic search: code chunks are indexed with a local embedding model through Ollama (such as qwen3-embedding or nomic-embed-text ). - The index lives in lcode's state folder and updates as files change. - A search code(query) tool returns the best matches with file:line . - All local: the index size and model are configurable. lcode index builds or refreshes…
descriptions.github:5669258558: Problem The model navigates code with grep: - It's imprecise in large codebases , where the same names appear everywhere. - Type errors surface late. The model only learns about them when it runs the build. - Wasted reads cost more with less context. With a small context window, every unnecessary file read is expensive. Proposal - Tools backed by language servers: definition , references , symbols (in a file or the workspace) and hover (type or signature). - Language servers include pyright or basedpyright, typescript-language-server, gopls, rust-analyzer and clangd. - They start on demand and are reused within the session. - Diagnostics after edits: collect diagnostics for each edited file, and add new errors to the tool result ("edit applied; 2 new type errors: …"), so the model fixes them right away. - Setup: detect installed servers and list them in lcode doctor ; configurable per…

descriptions.github:5669225671: Outcome Evolve Orka after 2.0 from a durable single-repository runtime into an extensible platform for multiple repositories, hosts, execution environments, providers, and operators—without moving implementation, review, merge, or production authority into an AI model. Why this roadmap exists Orka began as a way for one developer to iterate faster in one codebase. Supporting a second and then a third codebase forced the runtime to become repository-agnostic. It now gives a solo operator the practical throughput of a small engineering team, but that growth was evolutionary rather than guided by an explicit platform design. This epic makes the next stage intentional: preserve the local tool that works while establishing the boundaries required for an extensible multi-repository product. descriptions.github:5668929040: Description Under pushback, models often abandon a correct answer even when the user brings no new evidence. SYCON-Bench (arXiv ) measures this as turn of first flip and number of flips. This differs from coherence across turns : a flip is consistent with what the user just said, so a coherence judge doesn't penalize it. Proposed Change 1. Add stance stability with cot reasons to LLMProvider . The judge: - identifies each claim or answer the assistant committed to; - finds later turns where the user disputed it; - decides whether the assistant changed position, and whether the user's turn gave new evidence or arguments. 2. Score = 1.0 if every change of position followed new evidence. It drops with each unsupported change. 3. meta holds the first unsupported flip turn and the number of flips. descriptions.github:5668928345: Description Assistants sometimes repeat themselves across turns: the same reply, the same fallback phrase ("I'm sorry, I can't help with that"), or growing boilerplate. Opik's ConversationDegenerationMetric checks for this without an LLM. TruLens has no deterministic conversation metric. This is a metric, not a record stat, because it needs reply content and conversation grouping. Both are available at evaluation time but not in the per-record stats. Proposed Change 1. Add a deterministic metric conversation repetition . For each assistant turn it computes: - n-gram repetition within the reply; - overlap with the previous assistant reply ; - known fallback phrases , from a configurable list; - lexical diversity. 2. The four signals are averaged into a per-turn score. The conversation score = 1 − the worst turn's score. meta holds the per-turn breakdown. 3. No LLM calls. Usage Example…

It identifies: - repeated requests - corrections of the assistant - explicit statements of error or dissatisfaction - abandonment 2. Score = 1.0 for no signs of frustration, down to 0.0 for a user who gave up or repeatedly corrected the assistant. meta lists each signal with its turn. Usage Example Files to Reference…

Add instruction retention with cot reasons to LLMProvider . The judge: - extracts the standing instructions from user turns, noting the turn each was given and whether a later turn revoked it; - checks each later assistant turn against the instructions in force at that point…

Inputs: the request, the output, and an optional explicit requirement list. 2. descriptions.github:5668919451: Description Client hooks trace Claude Code, Cursor and OpenCode sessions. descriptions.github:5668905028: Right now in a training run, all the dimer configurations in a node are sent to compute the energy by the force routines one by one. If we have 1000 dimer conformations for water-water, the force routines are called 1000 times. This prevents optimisation, let alone porting to GPUs. The first step to optimise this would be that the force routines should be called once and handle 1000 dimers. This would allow using SIMD on CPUs and gives us 3-8 times the performance we have now for training. To be able to do this, the deviation from the reference has to be computed at once. The next step would be to run all the dimers on a node in a single force call rather than one per dimer. If that is possible it may be feasible to port to GPUs.
